questions.question: If the average of two numbers is 12 and the product of the same two numbers is 119, then the difference of those two numbers is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average of two numbers = 12.

Product of the same two numbers = 119.

**Formula Used:**

Let the two numbers be x and y.

Average = (x + y) / 2

Product = x × y

**Calculation:**

Given, Average = 12 ⇒ (x + y) / 2 = 12

⇒ x + y = 24 ⇒ (1)

Given, Product = 119 ⇒ x × y = 119 ⇒ (2)

From equation (1), y = 24 - x

Substitute y in equation (2),

x × (24 - x) = 119

⇒ 24x - x² = 119

⇒ x² - 24x + 119 = 0

Solving the quadratic equation,

x² - 17x - 7x + 119 = 0

x(x - 17) - 7(x - 17) = 0

(x - 17)(x - 7) = 0

⇒ x = 17 or x = 7

If x = 17, then y = 7 (from y = 24 - x)

If x = 7, then y = 17 (from y = 24 - x)

Therefore, the difference of those two numbers = |x - y| = |17 - 7| = 10

**The difference of those two numbers is 10.**

questions.question: Two cyclists start at the same time from opposite ends of a 200 km long straight road. One cyclist travels at a speed of 20 km/h and the other at a speed of 30 km/h. How long will it take them to meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two moving bodies travel in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds.

Relative Speed = 20 + 30 = 50 km/h

Time = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 200 ÷ 50 = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d51f9772e4e40b1d61ccb8a992e1c22e1d835837894551f469db397e392a37ee.png] 

**Given:**

Total distance between the two cyclists (D) = 200 km

Speed of the first cyclist (S₁) = 20 km/h

Speed of the second cyclist (S₂) = 30 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (when moving in opposite directions) = S₁ + S₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 20 km/h + 30 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 km/h

⇒ Time taken to meet = 200 km ÷ 50 km/h

⇒ Time taken = 4 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 4 hours.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Directions)

When two bodies move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: SR = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: SR = |S₁ − S₂|.

Average Speed

When a journey involves different speeds, the Average Speed over the entire journey is given by: Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

questions.question: A hollow metal sphere of internal and external radii 5 cm and 6 cm, respectively, is melted into a solid cone of base radius 5.2 cm. What is the height (in cm, rounded off to 1 decimal place) of the cone?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A hollow metal sphere with internal radius = 5 cm and external radius = 6 cm is melted into a solid cone with base radius = 5.2 cm.

**Concept:**

The volume of the hollow sphere equals the volume of the solid cone.

**Formula Used:**

Volume of hollow sphere = (4/3)π(R³ - r³)

Volume of cone = (1/3)πr²h

**Calculation:**

We have:

⇒ External radius (R) = 6 cm

⇒ Internal radius (r) = 5 cm

⇒ Base radius of cone = 5.2 cm

Volume of hollow sphere:

⇒ Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = (4/3)π(R³ - r³)

⇒ Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = (4/3)π(6³ - 5³)

⇒ Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = (4/3)π(216 - 125)

⇒ Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = (4/3)π(91)

⇒ Vₛₚₕₑᵣₑ = (364/3)π

Volume of cone:

⇒ V꜀ₒₙₑ = (1/3)πr²h

⇒ (364/3)π = (1/3)π(5.2)²h

⇒ 364 = (5.2)²h

⇒ 364 = 27.04h

⇒ h = 364 / 27.04

⇒ h ≈ 13.5

**∴ The height of the cone is 13.5 cm.**

questions.question: If Rita's salary increases by 5% in the first year and by 2% in the next year, then what is the net percentage increase in her salary after two years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net percentage change for two successive increases of a% and b% is given by:

Net Increase % = a + b + (a × b)/100

Here, a = 5 and b = 2

Net Increase = 5 + 2 + (5 × 2)/100 = 7 + 0.1 = 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase in first year = 5%

Increase in second year = 2%

**Formula Used:**

Final Value = Initial Value × (1 + r₁/100) × (1 + r₂/100)

 
• 
 
 
 
 Initial (100)
 Year 1 (105)
 Year 2 (107.1)
 

 +5%
 

 +2%
 Net % Increase = 7.1%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial salary be 100.

⇒ Salary after 1st year = 100 + 5% of 100 = 105

⇒ Salary after 2nd year = 105 + 2% of 105

⇒ Salary after 2nd year = 105 + (2/100) × 105

⇒ Salary after 2nd year = 105 + 2.1 = 107.1

⇒ Net increase in salary = 107.1 − 100 = 7.1

⇒ Net percentage increase = (7.1/100) × 100 = 7.1%

**∴ The correct answer is 7.1%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Decrease

When a value decreases by a% and then by b%, the net decrease is given by: −a − b + (a × b)/100.

Mixed Change (Increase and Decrease)

If a value increases by a% and then decreases by b%, the net change is: a − b − (a × b)/100.

Fractional Method

Percentages can be converted to fractions (e.g., 5% = 1/20, 2% = 1/50) and multiplied as (1 + 1/20) × (1 + 1/50) to find the final multiplier.</p

questions.question: Mohan can complete a piece of work in 24 days. He worked for 6 days and left the work. Thereafter, Sohan finished the remaining work in 21 days. In how many days, can Mohan and Sohan together complete it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mohan can complete work in 24 days.

Mohan worked for 6 days and left the work.

Sohan completed the remaining work in 21 days.

**Formula Used:**

Work Done = Time × Efficiency

Total Work = LCM of individual times (if required)

Combined Efficiency = Total Work / Time taken by both to complete the work together

**Calculation:**

Let the total work be 24 units (assuming 1 unit of work is done by Mohan in 1 day).

Mohan's efficiency = 1 unit/day.

Mohan's work in 6 days = 6 units.

Remaining work = 24 - 6 = 18 units.

Sohan takes 21 days to complete 18 units.

Sohan's efficiency = 18 units / 21 days = (6)/(7) units/day.

Combined efficiency of Mohan and Sohan = 1 + (6)/(7) = (13)/(7) units/day.

Total work to be done = 24 units.

Time taken by Mohan and Sohan working together = Total Work / Combined Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = (24)/(frac{13){7}} = (24 times 7)/(13) 

⇒ Time taken = (168)/(13) days

⇒ Time taken = 12 (12)/(13) days

**Mohan and Sohan together can complete the work in 12 (12)/(13) days.**

Simple Interest (I) = (Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T)) / 100

**Calculation:**

questions.question: If the ratio among the time taken by three cars to travel a certain distance is 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5, then the ratio of speeds of these cars will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of time taken by three cars = 2 ∶ 3 ∶ 5

**Formula Used:**

Speed ∝ 1/Time (If distance is constant)

**Calculation:**

Let the speeds of the cars be S₁, S₂, and S₃ respectively.

Let the times taken by the cars be 2t, 3t, and 5t respectively.

Since speed = distance/time, if the distance is constant, then speed is inversely proportional to time.

Therefore, S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 1/(2t) ∶ 1/(3t) ∶ 1/(5t)

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 1/2 ∶ 1/3 ∶ 1/5

To remove the fractions, multiply each term by the LCM of the denominators (2, 3, 5) which is 30.

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = (30 × 1/2) ∶ (30 × 1/3) ∶ (30 × 1/5)

⇒ S₁ ∶ S₂ ∶ S₃ = 15 ∶ 10 ∶ 6

**The ratio of the speeds of these cars is 15 ∶ 10 ∶ 6.**

questions.question: Find the LCM of 1288, 230, 276.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers are 1288, 230, and 276.

**Formula Used:**

LCM (Least Common Multiple) of numbers.

**Calculation:**

Prime factorization of 1288 = 2³ × 7 × 23

Prime factorization of 230 = 2 × 5 × 23

Prime factorization of 276 = 2² × 3 × 23

LCM = Highest power of all prime numbers in the factorization

⇒ LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5 × 7 × 23

⇒ LCM = 8 × 3 × 5 × 7 × 23

⇒ LCM = 19320

**The LCM of 1288, 230, and 276 is 19320.**

questions.question: Arvind, Bilal, Carmen invest ₹49,000 towards a business. Arvind invests ₹5,000 more than Bilal and Bilal invests ₹4,000 more than Carmen. Out of a total profit of ₹98,000, how much does Bilal receive?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total investment by Arvind, Bilal, and Carmen = ₹49,000

Arvind invests ₹5,000 more than Bilal and Bilal invests ₹4,000 more than Carmen.

Total profit = ₹98,000

**Formula Used:**

If A, B, and C invests x, y, and z respectively in a business, then the profit is distributed among them in the ratio of their investments i.e., x:y:z.

**Calculation:**

Let Carmen's investment be ₹c.

⇒ Bilal's investment = ₹(c + 4,000)

⇒ Arvind's investment = ₹(c + 4,000 + 5,000) = ₹(c + 9,000)

Total investment = c + (c + 4,000) + (c + 9,000) = ₹49,000

⇒ 3c + 13,000 = 49,000

⇒ 3c = 36,000

⇒ c = 12,000

Therefore, Carmen's investment = ₹12,000, Bilal's investment = ₹12,000 + 4,000 = ₹16,000, and Arvind's investment = ₹12,000 + 9,000 = ₹21,000.

Ratio of their investments = 12,000:16,000:21,000 = 12:16:21

Total ratio = 12 + 16 + 21 = 49

Bilal's share of the profit = (16 / 49) × 98,000

⇒ Bilal's share = 2,000 × 16 = ₹32,000

**Bilal receives ₹32,000.**

questions.question: The average weight of some students in class 12th was 56 kg. When seven students whose average weight was 58 kg joined the class, the average weight of all the students increased by 200 gm. Find the number of students in the class in the beginning?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of students initially is 56 kg.

Seven students with an average weight of 58 kg joined.

The average weight increased by 200 gm (0.2 kg).

**Concept Used:**

Weighted average and basic algebra.

**Formula Used:**

Total weight of initial students = (number of students) × (average weight)

New average weight = (total weight of all students) / (total number of students)

**Calculation:**

Let the initial number of students be x

⇒ Total initial weight = 56 × x

⇒ Total weight of new students = 58 × 7

⇒ Total weight after new students join = 56 × x + 58 × 7

⇒ New average weight = (56 × x + 58 × 7) / (x + 7)

⇒ New average weight = 56 + 0.2

⇒ (56 × x + 58 × 7) / (x + 7) = 56.2

⇒ 56 × x + 406 = 56.2 × (x + 7)

⇒ 56 × x + 406 = 56.2 × x + 393.4

⇒ 406 - 393.4 = 56.2 × x - 56 × x

⇒ 12.6 = 0.2 × x

⇒ x = 12.6 / 0.2

⇒ x = 63

**∴ The number of students in the class at the beginning was 63.**
